name: S_4 wr AGL(3,2) x S_3
description: SMALLEST INSTANCE FOUND, m=32: the previous group together with the full S_3 on the three leftover points 32,33,34. Order 24^8 * 1344 * 6 = 887647333515264, only 12 orbits on the 4-subsets. Usability is non-obvious and rests on the fact that for every 5-subset W of AG(3,2) the sum of W lies IN W (the complement is a 3-set {x,y,z} and x+y+z is not in {x,y,z}), so exactly one of the five faces is an affine plane and four are not, and the five faces are never all in one orbit
family: Z_m acting on m points with the remaining 35-m points fixed pointwise (m = 31,32,33,34)

name: S_4 wr AGL(3,2)

Order 24^8 * 1344 = 147941222252544. Compact 5-generator set (S_4 on block 0 only, plus 3 block-group gens; conjugation spreads S_4 to every block since the block group is transitive) VERIFIED identical to the redundant 21-generator set; 32,33,34 fixed

name: AGL(3,2)
description: Affine group of AG(3,2), order 1344, induced on the 35 bisections. Identify {0..7} with F_2^3 by binary digits (bit i = coefficient of e_i). Generators on 8 points: translation x -> x XOR 1 (i.e. x + e_0); the coordinate 3-cycle e_0->e_1->e_2->e_0, x -> ((x<<1)|(x>>2)) & 7; and the transvection e_0 -> e_0+e_1, x -> x XOR ((x&1)<<1). The last two generate GL(3,2) of order 168; adding one translation gives all of AGL(3,2) since GL(3,2) is transitive on nonzero vectors. Verified: transitive on the 8 points, |stab(0)| = 168, 2-transitive, contained in A_8. It is a MAXIMAL subgroup of A_8 (all 15 cosets checked: <AGL(3,2), g> = A_8 for every g in A_8 outside it) and self-normalising in S_8 (|N_{S_8}(AGL(3,2))| = 1344), so no 5'-subgroup of S_8 properly contains it -- this really is the ceiling.
family: 5'-subgroups acting on the 35 bisections (4+4 splits) of an 8-set = the 35 lines of PG(3,2)

THIS INSTANCE IS SATISFIABLE: a witness was found and independently verified (0 monochromatic K5^(4) among all 324632 five-subsets of the 35 points, G-invariance confirmed, colour balance 25432/26928)

name: S_4 wr S_2
description: The full stabiliser of one bisection of {0..7}, order 1152 = 40320/35 exactly, induced on the 35 bisections. Stabilised split is {0,1,2,3}|{4,5,6,7} = point 0. Generators on 8 points: (0 1) = [1,0,2,3,4,5,6,7]; (0 1 2 3) = [1,2,3,0,4,5,6,7]; and the half-swap (0 4)(1 5)(2 6)(3 7) = [4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3]. The first two generate S_4 on the first half; the half-swap conjugates that onto the second half and supplies the top S_2, so these three generate the full wreath product. Verified: order 1152, transitive on the 8 points, |stab(0)| = 144 = S_3 x S_4, NOT 2-transitive (it preserves the split, as it must), not contained in A_8. 1152 = 2^7 * 3^2, coprime to 5.

name: A-Gamma-L(1,8)
description: Semilinear affine group of F_8, order 168, induced on the 35 bisections. Identify {0..7} with F_8 = F_2[t]/(t^3+t+1) (integer bits = coefficients of 1, t, t^2; reduction mask 0b1011). Generators on 8 points: x -> x+1 (i.e. x XOR 1); x -> t*x (carryless multiply by 2 mod t^3+t+1), which is a 7-cycle since t is primitive; and the Frobenius x -> x^2, of order 3. Verified: order 168 = 8*7*3, transitive on the 8 points, |stab(0)| = 21 = Gamma-L(1,8) = C_7 : C_3, 2-transitive, contained in A_8. Note this is a DIFFERENT group of order 168 from PSL(3,2) -- it is soluble (Frobenius-by-C_3), not simple.

name: PSL(3,2)
description: GL(3,2) = PSL(3,2) = Fano-plane collineation group of order 168, realised on {0..6} by identifying base point i with the nonzero vector of F_2^3 whose bit pattern is i+1 (i.e. v = (b0,b1,b2), i+1 = b0 + 2*b1 + 4*b2), then induced on the 35 triples. Base generators on {0..6}: g1 = multiplication by x in F_8 = F_2[x]/(x^3+x+1), i.e. (a0,a1,a2) -> (a2, a0+a2, a1), which is [1,3,5,2,0,6,4] (order 7); g2 = the transvection a0 += a1, i.e. [0,2,1,3,4,6,5] (order 2). Point orbits on the 35 triples are the 7 Fano lines and the 28 non-lines. Largest usable group in this family, and provably the largest 5'-subgroup of S_7 -- smallest SAT instance available here: 374 variables.
